verdict.rationale: Better Auth markets 'Auth for AI agents' with token exchange and agent delegation. Its API Key plugin issues separately managed keys, including organization-owned ones, with custom expiration and rate limits. The MCP plugin also makes an app an OAuth authorization server for agent clients. That gives first-party machine credentials distinct from a human's login, but scoping and revocation for those credentials are not shown. missing for 10: documented per-key/per-agent scoped permissions, documented instant revocation of agent keys or tokens, detail on the agent delegation/token exchange mechanics, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give each agent its own least-privilege machine identity with narrowly scoped permissions and instant revocation, instead of sharing a human's credentials

citations.quote: Auth for AI agents. MCP auth, token exchange, and agent delegation.
Create, manage, and verify API keys ... Built-in rate limiting ... Custom expiration times, remaining count, and refill systems
Organization-owned API keys in addition to user-owned keys
The MCP plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for Model Context Protocol clients.
